name: sedan_cvt
source: Plausible push-belt CVT with a torque converter and lock-up clutch for a 2.0 L passenger car. Variator [AS], NOT a specific gearbox: steel push belt, ratio 2.63 (launch) to 0.38 (overdrive), spread ~6.9, in the range of current passenger push-belt CVTs (spreads 5.5-7.3; e.g. Naunheimer et al., Automotive Transmissions, 2nd ed., Springer 2011, ch. 6, and Srivastava/Haque, A review on belt and chain CVT, Mech. Mach. Theory 2009 - verify before citing). Ratio rate 1.2 ln-units/s continuous, 6.0 between the seven virtual steps of the stepped mode [AS]. Efficiency 0.86 at launch ratio, 0.92 near 1:1, 0.90 in overdrive [AS] (published push-belt CVT mechanical efficiencies 0.85-0.93). Pump drag 2 N*m + 0.08 N*m per kN clamping force [AS]. Belt [AS]: traction coefficient 0.09, sheave half angle 11 deg, drive+driven running radius 0.2 m, clamping force 4-45 kN with safety factor 1.3 over max(input torque, engine demand) and a 50 ms lag: belt capacity ~455 N*m at the launch ratio and the maximum force, ~1.4x the converter's stall turbine torque against the 2.0 L sedan engine. Reverse -2.60 (planetary reverse x launch ratio) [AS]. CVT plan C1. Converter copied from sedan_8at [AS]; forward/reverse clutch 450 N*m kinetic [AS].
